title: Generic Enums
concept: Generic enums like Option[T] and Result[T, E] are the foundation of XIOM's error handling — parameterized over the types they contain.
why: Without generic enums, you'd need separate OptionInt, OptionStr, OptionBool types. Generic enums give you one abstraction for all types.
tips: Generic enums are most useful for sum types: Option, Result, Either, Tree
Use descriptive type parameter names: T for value, E for error, K for key, V for value
Enum variants with no data (like None) don't need type parameters
The compiler ensures you handle all variants when pattern matching
common_mistakes: Confusing Option and Result — Option for presence/absence, Result for success/failure
Forgetting that None() needs empty parentheses
Using generic enums where a simple struct would suffice — don't over-complicate
